cli.finalMessage:
This looks correct and complete. The screen is built with:

- **Card header**: name, network, and last four digits (with a screen-reader-friendly full description).
- **Freeze control**: always enabled, prominent switch at the top.
- **Frozen state**: shows a status banner and wraps the other controls in a `<fieldset disabled>`, which natively disables the toggle switches and slider and dims/blocks interaction via CSS — so it's clear (and enforced) that they don't apply until unfrozen.
- **Toggles**: online payments, contactless, international use, each with icon, title, description, and an accessible custom switch (`role="switch"`, RTL-safe via logical CSS properties).
- **Daily limit slider**: native range input ($100–$10,000, live value display).

Styling uses Strata design tokens (`var(--strata-color-...)`, `var(--strata-space-...)`, etc.) with sensible fallbacks, and logical CSS properties throughout so it adapts to dark mode and RTL locales automatically. All mock data lives in `Screen.tsx`; no other files were touched.
